capabilities.title: AuthZEN evaluation endpoint
capabilities.summary: POST /api/v1/access/evaluation is the AuthZEN-native adapter over the same evaluation /api/v1/decide serves, registered in every edition at every tier with no flag and no kill switch.

health.name: authzen_evaluation
health.description: AuthZEN-native authorization on POST /api/v1/access/evaluation. A PEP sends the AuthZEN envelope in either shape (a singular `evaluation` or a plural `evaluations`, exactly one member, enforced by the decoder, the JSON Schema and every generated client alike) and gets back ONE decision: the entries of a plural envelope are preconditions of a single operation, so they meet, and one denied entry denies the operation. Profile negotiation is the X-Axonflow-AuthZEN-Profile request header. No header (or an empty one) means the caller asked for AuthZEN 1.0 and gets exactly that, the bare boolean - with ONE exception, which a PEP feature-detecting this surface must handle: an otherwise-ALLOWED decision carrying a MANDATORY obligation answers such a caller with the boolean false, because the obligation rides in the context it did not negotiate and it must not be handed a permission whose precondition it will never see (ADR-065 invariant 8; the denial is counted under outcome=obligation_withheld and audited as blocked with policy_details.authzen_obligation_withheld). An allow carrying no mandatory obligation is still true for a bare caller, and the denied, challenged and errored paths are unchanged. `axonflow-authzen-profile-2026-08-29` additionally returns the AxonFlow rendering in the response context: four-valued operational state, obligations, safe reason. What it does NOT carry is an approval challenge, and that is stated rather than left to be discovered: this route is an ADAPTER over POST /api/v1/decide, whose response names no eligible approver set, no quorum and no challenge expiry, so there is no requirement to render and inventing one would hand an enforcement point a fabricated approval policy. A decision awaiting approval is reported as state CHALLENGE with decision:false, which a PEP acts on by holding rather than executing; the challenge itself is obtained from the HITL surfaces. Earlier text here promised the challenge on this surface and no response ever carried one (#3631). Any other non-empty profile is REFUSED, naming the profile this build emits, so a PEP negotiating a later profile against an older server can never read a bare allow as a successful negotiation and proceed past an obligation it never saw. Refusals raised before evaluation are typed and carry a JSON pointer to the offending member: malformed_envelope, incomplete_evaluation, unsupported_subject, unsupported_action, unsupported_resource, unevaluable_attribute, missing_evaluable_content, evaluation_unavailable. This route is an ADAPTER over the evaluation POST /api/v1/decide already serves, NOT the ADR-065 Policy Decision Point: the envelope is mapped to a DecideRequest and run through that same handler, so the two surfaces cannot drift, /api/v1/decide is unchanged and wire-stable, and at v11 the engine behind this route changes with no wire change. Registered unconditionally in every edition at every tier, with no flag and no kill switch; audit rows from this surface record plane `access_evaluation` so adoption is measurable separately from /api/v1/decide (ADR-065, #3611)

capabilities.title: PEP capability handshake
capabilities.summary: An enforcement point declares, per governed request, the obligation types and schema versions it can DISCHARGE, in the X-Axonflow-PEP-Handshake header; a MANDATORY obligation the declaration does not cover is refused instead of emitted.

health.name: pep_capability_handshake
health.description: Declare, on every governed call, the obligation types and schema versions this enforcement point can DISCHARGE, as a base64url-encoded compact JSON document in the X-Axonflow-PEP-Handshake request header. The header is OPTIONAL and ABSENT IS NOT EMPTY: no header is the legacy caller and is byte-for-byte today's behaviour, while a header present with an empty value is malformed and refuses. Read on three planes and one vocabulary serves all three, so one declaration satisfies them all: POST /api/v1/decide (and the AuthZEN adapter over it), the MCP plane (/api/v1/mcp/check-input, /api/v1/mcp/check-output and the MCP server's check tools), and the gateway pre-check plane (POST /api/policy/pre-check). WHAT A DECLARATION MEANS: discharging field_redact@1 is substituting the platform's engine-masked content for the original, which ADR-056 makes the only sanctioned discharge because a client may not redact for itself - so a client that performs no substitution declares the EMPTY SET and is denied rather than allowed on the strength of a discharge nobody performs. A mandatory obligation outside the declared set is refused with reason pep_capability_unsupported, and the refusal withholds the instruction as well as the content. The three planes reach that refusal differently and a PEP integrating against one must not assume the others: decide EMITS an obligation naming a fulfillment endpoint, the MCP plane IS that endpoint and returns masked text inline, and pre-check issues an INSTRUCTION (requires_redaction) which is cleared on a refusal. Structural refusals are their own reasons and are not capability refusals: pep_handshake_malformed (unreadable document), pep_handshake_identity_unbindable (the authenticated channel carries no client identity, so the declaration cannot be bound to a name the server owns), pep_handshake_edition_unresolvable. A capability claimed beyond what this deployment's edition can hold is DROPPED rather than refused and the request proceeds on the narrowed set. Every outcome is counted, absence included, because a window with no malformed handshakes is equally well explained by a correct fleet and by a fleet presenting nothing. EDITION SPLIT: presenting, validating, binding, narrowing and counting a declaration happen in every edition; turning an uncoverable mandatory obligation into a deny the platform can see, audit and count is Enterprise, and a Community build hands the obligation over exactly as it does today, where the enforcement point fails closed at its own seam (ADR-065 invariant 8, ADR-066 decision 5)

capabilities.notes: ADR-066 decision 5 split with BOTH halves operational, which is why the classification is community_core and not enterprise_protocol: platform/agent/pep_handshake.go and the whole read/validate/bind/narrow/count path compile into a Community build unconditionally, and what sits behind the tag is the DECIDING half - THREE files, one per plane (pep_handshake_enforce_enterprise.go, pep_handshake_mcp_enforce_enterprise.go, pep_handshake_precheck_enforce_enterprise.go), each with a !enterprise twin that returns the verdict untouched. (The design document calls the wire contract enterprise_protocol; in THIS registry's vocabulary that classification means source kept OUT of a Community build, which is the opposite of what ships, and the validator refuses the pairing. Same shape as license.validation.) IMPLEMENTATION LISTS ALL NINE FILES UNDER platform/agent, not just the decide plane's three: the edition-fact derivation walks exactly the paths listed here, and the backstop that catches a trimmed list is scoped to route-REGISTERING files - which this capability deliberately has none of, so a short list would be checked by nothing. The cap on the two lower editions is the DENY, and only the deny: the three community twins return the verdict untouched, so those builds emit the mandatory obligation anyway - today's behaviour, where the enforcement point fails closed at its own seam rather than forwarding ungoverned content. The structural refusals (pep_handshake_malformed, pep_handshake_identity_unbindable, pep_handshake_edition_unresolvable) and the over-advertisement narrowing DO fire in every edition; community mode is in fact the one deployment class where the over-advertising rule can fire at all. OWNER names the decide plane's test because the field takes one path. It is one of ELEVEN: pep_handshake_test.go, pep_handshake_mcp_test.go and pep_handshake_precheck_test.go for the three planes' shared halves; each plane's enforcement half under its own _enforce_{community,enterprise}_test.go pair, six more; plus pep_handshake_authzen_test.go and pep_handshake_openapi_contract_test.go. Counted with `ls`, because an earlier revision of this sentence said seven and its own enumeration came to nine. No route of its own: the header is read on routes governance.decide, the MCP capabilities and the gateway pre-check already own, which is why this entry claims planes and not routes.

capabilities.title: Seam-capability-aware obligations
capabilities.summary: A PEP advertises what its seam can discharge and the engine emits only obligations that caller can fulfil, applying the org's fallback posture.

health.name: seam_capability_decisioning
health.description: Seam-capability-aware obligations: a PEP advertises what its seam can discharge via DecideRequest.fulfillment_capabilities (vocabulary: request_body_redaction, request_header_mutation) and POST /api/v1/decide emits only obligations that caller can fulfill. A request-body redaction suppressed on a non-capable seam (e.g. Envoy ext_authz, which is headers-only) applies the org's obligation-fallback posture — log (default: allow, no obligation, canonical audit row records the suppressed redaction + detected categories) or block (deny) — configurable per org on the obligation_fallback detection-posture category. The posture is resolved server-side from the org, never from the request; absent/empty capabilities means a legacy caller and reproduces pre-9.11.0 behavior exactly (all SDKs unaffected). Replaces the adapter-local allow→403 conversion so every outcome is an engine round-trip (ADR-056)

capabilities.title: Per-client version telemetry
capabilities.summary: Validated X-Axonflow-Client id and version pairs are recorded into the axonflow_client_version_requests_total counter.

health.name: client_version_telemetry
health.description: Per-client version-distribution telemetry: validated X-Axonflow-Client client id + version pairs are recorded into the axonflow_client_version_requests_total counter on the decide and MCP check-output planes (Enterprise builds; Community builds no-op and register no series). Since 10.4.0 the counter also carries `deployment_mode` and `licensed`, which say what kind of deployment the fleet reading the counter is. BOTH ARE PROCESS PROPERTIES RESOLVED SERVER-SIDE, never read from a request — a label a caller could influence would let one client rewrite the population every other series is read against. `deployment_mode` is this binary's own DEPLOYMENT_MODE resolved through the canonical map (aliases folded; an unset variable reports `unset`, which is deliberately NOT `community`, and an unrecognised value reports `unknown`); `licensed` is `true` only once the licence validator has resolved a non-Community tier, so the boot window and an unlicensed enterprise build both report `false`. READ THE POPULATION BEFORE READING THE NUMBERS: the counter exists only on Enterprise builds, so `deployment_mode` here can never observe a Community BUILD and this metric structurally cannot answer "how many Community installs exist" — it answers "which modes do our Enterprise-build deployments run as". Telemetry-only — never consulted for auth or a verdict

capabilities.notes: Enterprise builds only: the community build no-ops and registers no series. ADVERTISED ON /health IN EVERY EDITION, so a community deployment claims a counter it does not export.
